category_title: Five-year-old students exhibiting school-related frustration and challenging peer interactions
minimal_context: Patrick is arriving at the classroom in the morning and needs to transition into a classroom activity.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Good morning. It is time to come into the classroom and pick an activity to do while the other children are working.

STUDENT: School is dumb. I want to go home.

TUTOR: I am sure we can find something you might like to do here.

STUDENT: I am upset I could not bring my Power Rangers to school.

TUTOR: We have interesting materials in the classroom you can interact with instead.

STUDENT: (Kicks the furniture in frustration) No! I want to go home!

options.A: Send a clear message to Patrick regarding the tutor's dissatisfaction with his behavior of kicking the classroom furniture during the morning arrival transition.
options.B: Engage Patrick in a conversation about what he wants to do, validate his feelings about the Power Rangers, and explain that they can find something he might like.
options.C: Provide Patrick with a detailed instruction of each specific element involved in choosing and completing a morning classroom activity during the arrival period.
options.D: Give Patrick a warning first, followed by a 10-minute timeout in the classroom if he does not stop kicking the furniture during the transition.
